$note: Standard statements of named theorems, laws and definitions, read by scripts/qa/shingles.mjs. A run that lies inside one of these is reported as "allowed" rather than as a stimulus-copy breach: a theorem in its standard form is common mathematical or scientific language, not the board's stimulus writing, and there is no honest way to say it differently. Every entry is one standard statement with the reason it qualifies. Add an entry ONLY for a named law, theorem or definition; a context sentence, a question setup or a table of values is never allowed here however often the board reuses it, and an exam instruction belongs in the script's STANDING_PHRASES, not here. Keys beginning with $ are ignored.
A tangent to a circle is perpendicular t: circle theorem, M4-GM-02 ('angle between tangent and radius'); the standard statement, and M8-NA-12's Teacher Guidance uses the same words
The angle in a semicircle is a right ang: circle theorem, M4-GM-02 ('angle in a semicircle')
The angle at the centre is twice the ang: circle theorem, M4-GM-02 ('angle at the centre and at the circumference')
Angles in the same segment are equal: circle theorem, M4-GM-02 ('angles in the same segment')
Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilatera: circle theorem, M4-GM-02 ('cyclic quadrilaterals'): the same theorem in its other standard wording ('in' for 'of'), the form the textbooks and the M4 schemes print as the reason to give (25 Sep)
y is inversely proportional to the squar: the standard statement of an inverse-square relationship (M8 proportion); the relationship has one accepted English form, so any wording of it repeats the board's
Dynamic equilibrium occurs in a closed s: the definition of dynamic equilibrium, CCEA Double Award specification 2.4.2 (Higher), which the C2 Higher mark schemes credit in these words; a definition has one accepted English form, and the answer key words must accept it in the form she is taught to write it (c2-equilibrium, 22 Sep)
